subject: northern snakehead
title: A Fish That Eats Birds and Crawls on Land Reached a US Pond. They Poisoned It

scenes.text: This fish eats birds, breathes air, and crawls to the next pond when it's done.
The northern snakehead, from China and Korea. Nearly three feet long, with a mouth full of sharp teeth.
Its swim bladder works like a lung. It can live out of water for four days and wriggle over land to the next pond.
It eats fish, frogs, birds and small mammals. It survives under ice. In America, nothing hunts it.
In 2002, one turned up in a Maryland pond. A man had dumped two fish from a New York market. Biologists found 100 babies.
A river was 70 metres away. So they poisoned the entire pond. Too late. They've since turned up across two states.

description:
The northern snakehead can breathe air with a swim bladder that works like a primitive lung, survive up to four days out of water in damp spots, and wriggle over land between ponds. It grows to about 33 inches and eats fish, frogs, birds and small mammals.
In 2002 the first US breeding population was found in a pond in Crofton, Maryland, after a man released two fish bought at a New York market; biologists caught about 100 juveniles and, with a river only 70 metres away, poisoned the whole pond. Snakeheads have since turned up across Maryland and Pennsylvania.
Should invasive fish be eaten to control them? Comment below.

first_comment: The man said he bought the pair to eat, then changed his mind and set them free. Snakeheads tolerate water from freezing to 86 degrees Fahrenheit. Which invasive animal should we cover next?
